title: Salary Tier Label
description:
Label each employee with a salary tier:
- `'High'` if salary ≥ 100 000
- `'Mid'` if salary is between 60 000 and 99 999 (inclusive)
- `'Low'` if salary < 60 000

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| salary | INT |

Output columns: `name`, `salary`, `tier`. Order by `salary` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 120000), (2, 'Bob', 80000), (3, 'Carol', 140000), (4, 'Dan', 55000), (5, 'Eve', 90000);
solution_sql: SELECT name, salary, CASE WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 60000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Low' END AS tier FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC

test_cases.description: Carol and Alice are High; Eve and Bob are Mid; Dan is Low

hints: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END evaluates conditions top-to-bottom.
The first matching WHEN wins — so put the highest threshold first.
explanation: CASE works like an if/else chain. Because `>= 100000` is checked first, salaries of 120000 and 140000 get 'High'. The next branch catches 60000–99999 ('Mid'). ELSE catches everything below 60000 ('Low').
